newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa prime seen steady for next 3 mths -survey.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa prime seen steady for next 3 mths -survey.

text.p: South Africa's prime interest rate will likely remain unchanged in the next three months but money market and bond yields should ease, WorldGroup Banking said in its latest monthly interest rate forecast.
Economists participating in the forecast expected the 90-day BA rate to trade between 15.45 percent and 16.20 percent, with a most likely value of 15.85 percent.
The 12 month NCD rate was seen in a 15.55 to 16.55 percent range with an expected value of 16.15 percent while the most likely value for government's Eskom 168 stock was seen at 14.88 percent.
The 90-day BA rate is currently trading between 15.75 and 15.90 percent while 12 month NCD rates were last quoted at 16.40 percent offered.
On the bond market, the E168 stock was last trading at a 15.14 percent yield.
The half year scenario to October sees all rates easing with prime -- currently at 20.25 percent -- expected down 25 points to 20.00 percent and possibly a full percent to 19.25 percent.
The 90-day BA rate is forecast at 15.50 percent, in a band between 14.95 percent and 16.05 percent.
Twelve month NCD rates are seen 75 points lower at 15.80 percent or even as low as 15.05 percent.
Six economists -- Absa's Adam Jacobs, Nedcor's Dennis Dykes, Citadel's Louis Fourie, Transnet's Ulrich Joubert, Iscor's Kau Msimango and Huysamer Stals' Johan Roussouw -- took part in the survey.
The economists said the overall pattern showed that interest rates would remain stable initially but start a slow decline over the coming months.
They noted that demand for credit in particular remained high although this was expected to ease with the slowdown in the economy.
"Liquidity will continue to improve in line with the improvement in the current account balance and significant capital inflows," they said.
But the easing of exchange controls on July 1 remained a potential issue, especially in view of the low level of foreign exchange reserves.
